title: An Abortion Rights Champion of the 1970s on Life Before and After Roe

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普林，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代我在夜店打碟的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，你把DJ台变成了一个充满活力的、由美丽且有50年历史的艺术品组成的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在即可在你喜爱的播客平台上收听由爱彼呈现的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布里纳·塔韦尼西。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: 50 years ago, before Roe v.
sentences.zh: 50年前，在罗诉

sentences.en: Wade, a young lawyer in New York named Nancy Stearns brought a different case with a radical argument that the right to abortion was fundamental to equal rights for women.
sentences.zh: 韦德案之前，纽约一位名叫南希·斯特恩斯的年轻女律师提起了一起不同的诉讼，提出了一个激进的论点，即堕胎权是女性平权不可或缺的基础。

sentences.en: Today, Nancy Stearns on what it was like being on the front lines of the abortion fight at its beginning and how it feels to see that right fall.
sentences.zh: 今天，南希·斯特恩斯将讲述身处堕胎权之争最初前线时的感受，以及看到这一权利陨落时的心情。

sentences.en: It's Friday, July 1St.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月1日，星期五。

sentences.en: So, Nancy, I want to go back to the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 那么，南希，我想回到最初的时候。

sentences.en: How did you get involved in the cause of abortion rights?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么参与到争取堕胎权的运动中去的？

sentences.en: What drew you to it?
sentences.zh: 是什么吸引了你？

sentences.en: Well, it was the summer of 1963, June of 63.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是1963年的夏天，63年6月。

sentences.en: The summer that I finished my master's degree, I drove south with a friend of mine.
sentences.zh: 在我完成硕士学位的那个夏天，我和一个朋友开车去了南方。

sentences.en: And we thought, you know, we were going down just to do some volunteer work briefly with SNCC, the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee, to assist the civil rights movement.
sentences.zh: 我们当时想，你知道的，我们去那儿只是为了和学生非暴力协调委员会（SNCC）一起做一些短暂的志愿者工作，以协助民权运动。

sentences.en: Working with the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee are characterized by restless energy, radical change in race relations in the United States.
sentences.zh: 与学生非暴力协调委员会一起工作具有不息的活力，推动着美国种族关系的激进变革。

sentences.en: And rather than staying for the summer, I stayed for a year.
sentences.zh: 我没有只待一个夏天，而是待了一年。

sentences.en: By the forces of our demand, our determination, and our numbers, we shall splinter the segregated South into a thousand pieces.
sentences.zh: 凭借我们的诉求、我们的决心和我们的力量，我们将把实行隔离的南方击得粉碎。

sentences.en: It was really exciting to be part of a movement for social change, of something really important.
sentences.zh: 能够参与一场旨在实现社会变革、具有如此重大意义的运动，真的令人兴奋。

sentences.en: Being down there, I realized if I really wanted to be of greater value, it seemed to me the skill that made the most sense was a law degree.
sentences.zh: 身处那里，我意识到如果我真的想发挥更大的价值，对我来说最合理的技能就是一个法学学位。

sentences.en: So I went to law school.
sentences.zh: 于是我去读了法学院。

sentences.en: And when I was out of law school, somebody I knew suggested that I meet with a group of women from an organization called HealthPAC, the Health Policy Advisory Committee.
sentences.zh: 当我从法学院毕业后，我认识的一个人建议我跟一个来自“HealthPAC”（健康政策咨询委员会）组织的女性团体见个面。

sentences.en: And they met together in the evenings to talk about health issues as they related to women.
sentences.zh: 她们在晚上聚在一起，讨论与女性相关的健康问题。

sentences.en: And that's really, I think, what led me to being involved in the women's movement.
sentences.zh: 我想，正是这让我真正走上了投身妇女运动的道路。

sentences.en: I saw it, the women's movement, in the context of the civil rights movement.
sentences.zh: 我将妇女运动置于民权运动的语境中来看待。

sentences.en: Sex and race, because they are easy, visible differences, have been the primary ways of organizing human beings into superior and inferior groups.
sentences.zh: 由于性别和种族是容易察觉的、显而易见的差异，它们一直是将人类划分为优等群体和劣等群体的首要方式。

sentences.en: I could understand by what I was hearing and seeing and reading that women needed a movement just like the civil rights movement, just like Black people needed a movement.
sentences.zh: 我从我所听到、看到和读到的内容中能够理解，女性需要一场运动，就像民权运动一样，就像黑人需要一场运动一样。

sentences.en: Because we were not totally equal citizens.
sentences.zh: 因为我们并非完全平等的公民。

sentences.en: And our freedoms were very much restricted.
sentences.zh: 我们的自由受到了极大的限制。

sentences.en: And the scope of our lives were very much restricted.
sentences.zh: 我们生活的范围也受到了极大的限制。

sentences.en: Well, the main demand, of course, is equal rights.
sentences.zh: 嗯，主要的要求当然是平权。

sentences.en: Equal rights to have a job, to have respect, to not be viewed as a piece of meat.
sentences.zh: 拥有工作的平等权利，获得尊重的平等权利，不被视为一件商品的平等权利。

sentences.en: Equal rights to set forth our own humanity.
sentences.zh: 阐述我们自身人性的平等权利。

sentences.en: Equal rights.
sentences.zh: 平等的权利。

sentences.en: And I think for the first time, I really started thinking I could be part of challenging laws which really, really restricted women's freedom.
sentences.zh: 我想这是我第一次开始思考，我可以参与挑战那些真正极大地限制女性自由的法律。

sentences.en: Not since the suffragettes fought for the right to vote has an issue been more critical to women than abortion.
sentences.zh: 自从女性先驱争取投票权以来，还没有哪个议题比堕胎对女性而言更为关键。

sentences.en: Obviously, it's a concern for all women.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，这是所有女性都关心的问题。

sentences.en: All women face the problem of forced childbearing.
sentences.zh: 所有女性都面临着被迫生育的问题。

sentences.en: What do you mean by forced childbearing?
sentences.zh: 你所说的被迫生育是什么意思？

sentences.en: Being forced to carry, to term an unwanted pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 被迫将一场不想要的怀孕维持到足月。

sentences.en: That is forced childbearing.
sentences.zh: 这就是被迫生育。

sentences.en: So, how do you understand the connection between feminism and abortion?
sentences.zh: 那么，你是如何理解女性主义与堕胎之间的联系的？

sentences.en: I mean, why did abortion become the central cause to the women's movement?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么堕胎会成为妇女运动的核心诉求？

sentences.en: It's because if you cannot control your reproductive life, you cannot control your life.
sentences.zh: 这是因为如果你不能控制自己的生育生活，你就无法控制自己的生活。

sentences.en: And at that point, if you became pregnant, you could lose your job.
sentences.zh: 在那个时候，如果你怀孕了，你可能会失去工作。

sentences.en: If you became pregnant, you could lose your scholarship.
sentences.zh: 如果你怀孕了，你可能会失去奖学金。

sentences.en: You could be thrown out of your family.
sentences.zh: 你可能会被赶出家门。

sentences.en: You could have a child you couldn't raise, you couldn't pay for.
sentences.zh: 你可能会生下一个你无力抚养、无力支付费用的孩子。

sentences.en: I mean, it impacted every bit of your life.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它影响了你生活的方方面面。

sentences.en: And I knew that.
sentences.zh: 我很清楚这一点。

sentences.en: The more I knew, the more I knew that.
sentences.zh: 我知道得越多，就越深知这一点。

sentences.en: Nancy, at the time, what was the law in New York for abortion?
sentences.zh: 南希，当时纽约关于堕胎的法律是怎样的？

sentences.en: What did it say?
sentences.zh: 它具体规定了什么？

sentences.en: Abortion was prohibited in New York except to save the life of the woman.
sentences.zh: 纽约禁止堕胎，除非是为了挽救孕妇的生命。

sentences.en: It was one of the stricter ones.
sentences.zh: 这是最严厉的法律之一。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: But if you had the money to pay for two psychiatrists to say you were going to kill yourself if you
sentences.zh: 但如果你有钱支付两名精神科医生的费用，让他们证明如果你

sentences.en: were pregnant and had to carry the fetus to term, then you could get a legal abortion.
sentences.zh: 怀孕了却被迫将胎儿生下来，你就会自杀，那么你就可以通过合法途径堕胎。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So, how did you start thinking about addressing what you saw as an injustice here?
sentences.zh: 那么，你如何开始考虑解决你在这里看到的不公？

sentences.en: Up until then, the constitutionality of abortion laws had always been challenged in the context
sentences.zh: 在此之前，堕胎法的合宪性总是基于

sentences.en: of criminal prosecutions of doctors who performed abortions, or abortion counselors, people who referred women for abortions.
sentences.zh: 对实施堕胎的医生、堕胎咨询师或将女性转介去堕胎的人进行刑事起诉的背景下受到挑战。

sentences.en: And they would be prosecuted.
sentences.zh: 而他们会遭到起诉。

sentences.en: And they would raise constitutional questions to defend themselves.
sentences.zh: 并且他们会提出宪法问题来为自己辩护。

sentences.en: Normally, the major thing they would say was that the laws were too vague and therefore it
sentences.zh: 通常，他们提出的主要论点是法律过于含糊，因此

sentences.en: violated their right to due process and they couldn't know when they acted in some way whether they were violating the law.
sentences.zh: 侵犯了他们的正当程序权利，导致他们在以某种方式行事时无法知道自己是否在违法。

sentences.en: That was the main way laws were challenged.
sentences.zh: 这是挑战法律的主要方式。

sentences.en: Women were never in court themselves.
sentences.zh: 女性自己从未走上法庭。

sentences.en: It was as if we were irrelevant.
sentences.zh: 就好像我们无关紧要一样。

sentences.en: The relevant people were the doctors who were men and the abortion counselors who were primarily men but not exclusively men.
sentences.zh: 相关的人是身为男性的医生，以及主要是男性但并非全都是男性的堕胎咨询师。

sentences.en: And I felt like the crucial people who should be dealing with this and who should be challenging it are missing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得处理这件事并应该对此发起挑战的关键人物却缺席了。

sentences.en: And that was why I wanted to bring a lawsuit where, first of all, it would be affirmative.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我想提起诉讼，首先，它是主动出击的。

sentences.en: It wouldn't be defensive.
sentences.zh: 它不是防御性的。

sentences.en: It wouldn't be people defending themselves against prosecution.
sentences.zh: 它不是人们为了应对起诉而进行自我辩护。

sentences.en: It would be people going to court and saying, my rights are violated.
sentences.zh: 而是人们走进法庭说，我的权利受到了侵犯。

sentences.en: This is wrong.
sentences.zh: 这是不对的。

sentences.en: And this is why.
sentences.zh: 原因就在于此。

sentences.en: So how did you start going about doing that?
sentences.zh: 那你当时是怎么着手去做这件事的呢？

sentences.en: Well, women were beginning to get together talking about issues that affected their lives as women.
sentences.zh: 嗯，女性开始聚在一起，讨论那些作为女性影响她们生活的议题。

sentences.en: All of us are members of the Women's Liberation Group of New York City.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都是纽约市妇女解放运动小组成员。

sentences.en: And we thought when we were going to talk about abortion here tonight, instead of like just
sentences.zh: 我们当时想，今晚在这里讨论堕胎时，与其

sentences.en: talking about things that were really removed from us, we would talk about our own abortion.
sentences.zh: 只是谈论那些与我们相去甚远的事情，不如谈谈我们自己的堕胎经历。

sentences.en: What happened?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: So that would have been around 69.
sentences.zh: 所以那大概是在69年左右。

sentences.en: The man is the one that screws you.
sentences.zh: 搞大你肚子的是那个男人。

sentences.en: And then when you turn to him and say, hey, look, sweetheart, I'm pregnant.
sentences.zh: 然后当你转向他并说，嘿，听着，亲爱的，我怀孕了。

sentences.en: How do you know it was me?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道是我？

sentences.en: You never slept with anyone else?
sentences.zh: 你从来没和别人睡过吗？

sentences.en: Or he says, he holds his head and he says, what am I going to do?
sentences.zh: 或者他说，他抱着头说，我该怎么办？

sentences.en: What is he going to do?
sentences.zh: 他能怎么办？

sentences.en: What am I going to do?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么办？

sentences.en: That was a very important part of the women's movement, the development of the women's movement in the late 60s, early 70s.
sentences.zh: 那是妇女运动中非常重要的一部分，是60年代末70年代初妇女运动的发展。

sentences.en: When I went to get this abortion, like I knew what was happening.
sentences.zh: 当我去做这次堕胎时，我知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: I knew that I was going in and telling this psychiatrist that I was insane.
sentences.zh: 我知道我是去向这位精神科医生表明我疯了。

sentences.en: Because that's what you have to do.
sentences.zh: 因为那是你必须做的。

sentences.en: You have to tell him that you're going to commit suicide.
sentences.zh: 你必须告诉他你要自杀。

sentences.en: And you can't just say, no, look, doctor, I'm going to commit suicide.
sentences.zh: 你不能只是说，不，听着，医生，我要自杀。

sentences.en: You have to go and bring a razor or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你得去带一把剃须刀或者别的什么。

sentences.en: You know, if you don't give me, if you don't tell me I'm going to have an abortion right now, I'm going to go out and jump off the Verrazano Bridge or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你不让我，如果你不告诉我现在就能去堕胎，我就要跑出去从韦拉扎诺海桥上跳下去或者诸如此类。

sentences.en: But I knew what I was doing then.
sentences.zh: 但我当时很清楚自己在做什么。

sentences.en: And the summer of 1969 with the women from HealthPAC, what we ended up doing was having small group meetings around the city, all around the city.
sentences.zh: 1969年夏天，我和HealthPAC的女性成员们最终在全市各地召开了小组会议，遍布整个城市。

sentences.en: And we talked to women, you know, probably maybe 10 women, 15 women at a time.
sentences.zh: 我们和女性交谈，你知道的，大概每次10名女性，15名女性。

sentences.en: And that's what we did.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们当时做的事。

sentences.en: I would talk about abortion from a legal perspective and why I thought it was unconstitutional and what I thought we could do to challenge it.
sentences.zh: 我会从法律的角度谈论堕胎，为什么我认为它违宪，以及我认为我们可以采取什么行动来挑战它。

sentences.en: And then we would ask women if they wanted to talk about abortion and if they wanted to talk about their experiences with their doctors.
sentences.zh: 然后我们会问女性是否想谈论堕胎，以及是否想谈论她们与医生的经历。

sentences.en: And women really wanted to talk.
sentences.zh: 女性们真的很想倾诉。

sentences.en: And then we were able to say, do you want to be part of a group to try to do something about it?
sentences.zh: 接着我们就能问，你想加入一个团队，试着为此做点什么吗？

sentences.en: And people signed up to become plaintiffs to challenge the law as part of a larger group and seeing it in a larger political context.
sentences.zh: 人们报名成为原告，作为更大集体的一部分去挑战法律，并从更广泛的政治背景来看待它。

sentences.en: Okay, so you're hearing these stories of women who'd gone through illegal abortions.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以你听到了这些经历过非法堕胎的女性的故事。

sentences.en: How does that turn into a court case?
sentences.zh: 这怎么能变成一场诉讼呢？

sentences.en: A court case is stories.
sentences.zh: 一场诉讼就是故事。

sentences.en: A successful court case.
sentences.zh: 一场成功的诉讼。

sentences.en: Part of trying to build a case that says why all of these laws violate the Constitution and
sentences.zh: 构建一个论证所有这些法律如何违宪以及

sentences.en: violate women's rights is to talk about the details of the impact they had on women and then try to tie that to something the Constitution says.
sentences.zh: 侵犯女性权利的案件的一部分，就是谈论这些法律对女性产生影响的细节，然后试图将其与宪法条文联系起来。

sentences.en: That's the guts of it.
sentences.zh: 这才是核心所在。

sentences.en: It's people's lives.
sentences.zh: 这是人们的生活。

sentences.en: It's showing the impact that these laws that are wrong have on women's lives.
sentences.zh: 它展现了这些错误的法律对女性生活产生的影响。

sentences.en: I'm going to read you just a very short piece of the testimony of a woman who did not get an abortion.
sentences.zh: 我读一读一位没有堕胎的女性的证词中的一小段。

sentences.en: A woman who was a college student.
sentences.zh: 一个女大学生。

sentences.en: She had a scholarship.
sentences.zh: 她有奖学金。

sentences.en: She got pregnant.
sentences.zh: 她怀孕了。

sentences.en: She was not able to get an abortion.
sentences.zh: 她没能做成人工流产。

sentences.en: She lost her scholarship.
sentences.zh: 她失去了奖学金。

sentences.en: She was thrown out of college.
sentences.zh: 她被赶出了大学。

sentences.en: She ended up, well, let me just say how she said it.
sentences.zh: 她最终，嗯，让我直接用她的话来说吧。

sentences.en: The kind of trauma of giving a baby up for adoption leaves you with the feeling of a mother who's abandoned her child.
sentences.zh: 把孩子送去领养的那种创伤，会让你产生一种抛弃了自己孩子的母亲的感觉。

sentences.en: I prepared to think of myself as a breeder.
sentences.zh: 我把自己当成了一个生育机器。

sentences.en: I was just breeding babies for someone else to take rather than think of myself as a mother who had abandoned her baby.
sentences.zh: 我只是在为别人抚养而生育婴儿，而不是把自己当作一个抛弃了孩子的母亲。

sentences.en: But the guilt.
sentences.zh: 但是那种负罪感。

sentences.en: For months after I left the home for unwed mothers, I'd wake up in the nights crying and sort of rocking my pillow.
sentences.zh: 在我离开未婚母亲之家后的几个月里，我常常在夜里哭醒，甚至晃动着我的枕头。

sentences.en: To me, forcing a woman to do that is cruel and unusual punishment.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，迫使女性这样做是一种残酷且不寻常的惩罚。

sentences.en: That's one kind of story that you want to tell a judge who's never had to experience it or think of it or understand it.
sentences.zh: 这正是你想讲给那些从未经历过、思考过或理解过这一切的法官听的故事。

sentences.en: What that means in a woman's life.
sentences.zh: 这意味着女性生活中的什么。

sentences.en: And these stories became your case.
sentences.zh: 而这些故事成了你的案子。

sentences.en: They became, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，它们成为了。

sentences.en: Abramowitz versus Lefkowitz.
sentences.zh: 阿布拉莫维茨诉莱夫科维茨案。

sentences.en: The first abortion case I did in New York.
sentences.zh: 我在纽约办的第一起堕胎案。

sentences.en: So who was Abramowitz and who was Lefkowitz?
sentences.zh: 那么谁是阿布拉莫维茨，谁又是莱夫科维茨？

sentences.en: Tell me about the case.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲这个案子吧。

sentences.en: Lefkowitz was the attorney general of the state of New York.
sentences.zh: 莱夫科维茨是纽约州的总检察长。

sentences.en: Okay, what about Abramowitz?
sentences.zh: 好的，那阿布拉莫维茨呢？

sentences.en: Abramowitz, she was one of the many women.
sentences.zh: 阿布拉莫维茨，她是众多女性之一。

sentences.en: Her name started with A.
sentences.zh: 她的名字以A开头。

sentences.en: We put them in alphabetical order.
sentences.zh: 我们把她们按字母顺序排列。

sentences.en: So Abramowitz just happened to be first on the list of many plaintiffs.
sentences.zh: 所以阿布拉莫维茨恰好排在众多原告名单的第一位。

sentences.en: It was roughly 350 plaintiffs.
sentences.zh: 大约有350名原告。

sentences.en: So how did you make your case, Nancy?
sentences.zh: 那么南希，你是如何陈述你的案子的？

sentences.en: What was the focus of your argument before the court in this case?
sentences.zh: 在本案中，你在法庭上面对的辩论焦点是什么？

sentences.en: The way in which restrictive abortion laws violated women's liberty.
sentences.zh: 限制性堕胎法侵犯女性自由的方式。

sentences.en: How a woman could not live her life to the fullest if she lost her job when she became pregnant, if she got thrown out of school when she became pregnant,
sentences.zh: 女人如果在怀孕时失业，如果在怀孕时被学校开除，她的人生将如何无法尽情绽放，

sentences.en: if she couldn't take as good a job because of the restrictions on her hours.
sentences.zh: 如果她因为工时限制而无法从事同样好的工作。

sentences.en: All of those things have an impact on your liberty.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情都会对你的自由产生影响。

sentences.en: A woman could not be truly an equal member of society for the same reasons.
sentences.zh: 由于同样的原因，女性无法成为真正平等的社会成员。

sentences.en: If she couldn't get a full education, if she lost jobs, legislatures were virtually all male, courts were virtually all male.
sentences.zh: 如果她无法接受完整的教育，如果她失去了工作，立法机关几乎全是由男性组成，法院几乎全是由男性组成。

sentences.en: So a woman could not be part of the government mechanisms that ultimately made the decisions that controlled her life.
sentences.zh: 因此，女性无法参与最终做出控制其命运决策的政府机制。

sentences.en: That means you are not an equal member of the society.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你不是社会的平等成员。

sentences.en: So we were saying that not only was her right to liberty being violated, her right to the equal protection of the laws was being violated.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一直在说，不仅她的自由权受到了侵犯，她获得法律平等保护的权利也受到了侵犯。

sentences.en: And a woman doesn't create a fetus by herself.
sentences.zh: 而且胎儿不是女人一个人创造的。

sentences.en: A woman doesn't become pregnant by herself.
sentences.zh: 女人不是一个人就能怀孕的。

sentences.en: All of the limitations fall on a woman.
sentences.zh: 所有的限制都落在了女性身上。

sentences.en: A man can walk away and does often.
sentences.zh: 男人可以一走了之，而且经常这么做。

sentences.en: So that's a piece of it, too, the lack of equality, that there are two people that are creating this pregnancy and only one person, when it's unwanted,
sentences.zh: 所以这也是一部分，缺乏平等，制造这场怀孕的有两个人，而当它是意外怀孕时，只有一个人

sentences.en: has to bear the burden of it.
sentences.zh: 必须承担由此带来的负担。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And take the risks that childbirth entails.
sentences.zh: 并承担分娩带来的风险。

sentences.en: Nancy, how radical was that argument you were making at the time?
sentences.zh: 南希，你当时提出的那个论点有多激进？

sentences.en: I guess it was pretty radical.
sentences.zh: 我想这相当激进。

sentences.en: I mean, it just seemed common sense to me and to the other women that I explained it to.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对我以及我向其解释过它的其他女性来说，这似乎只是常识。

sentences.en: They understood.
sentences.zh: 她们理解了。

sentences.en: But I think even now it's obviously hard for some judges to understand it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为即使现在，某些法官显然也很难理解这一点。

sentences.en: We knew it.
sentences.zh: 我们知道。

sentences.en: We understood it in our gut.
sentences.zh: 我们从心底里理解它。

sentences.en: I was just translating it into legalese.
sentences.zh: 我只是把它翻译成了法律术语。

sentences.en: So, Nancy, it's 1970.
sentences.zh: 所以，南希，那是1970年。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What ends up happening to your case?
sentences.zh: 你的案子最后怎么样了？

sentences.en: We never really got there because of the change of the law.
sentences.zh: 由于法律的修改，我们实际上并没有走到那一步。

sentences.en: New York's assembly passed a bill legalizing abortions for any reason up to the 24th week of a pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 纽约州议会通过了一项法案，将在怀孕第24周之前以任何理由合法化堕胎。

sentences.en: The New York state legislature changes the law and makes abortion legal up until the last weeks of pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 纽约州立法机构修改了法律，使堕胎在怀孕最后几周之前合法化。

sentences.en: It's a huge change.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的改变。

sentences.en: It's a gargantuan change.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其巨大的改变。

sentences.en: Tomorrow, July 1st, abortion becomes legal in New York state.
sentences.zh: 明天，7月1日，堕胎在纽约州合法化。

sentences.en: And so that technically makes our case moot.
sentences.zh: 所以这从技术上讲使我们的案子失去了审理意义。

sentences.en: There is no longer a restrictive abortion law in New York to challenge.
sentences.zh: 纽约不再有需要质疑的限制性堕胎法了。

sentences.en: Health department officials predict a demand for between 50,000 and 100,000 abortions in New York City yearly.
sentences.zh: 卫生部门官员预测，纽约市每年对堕胎的需求在5万到10万次之间。

sentences.en: We've gotten calls from Texas, from Tennessee, from Florida, from New Hampshire, from Chicago, from Iowa.
sentences.zh: 我们接到了来自德克萨斯州、田纳西州、佛罗里达州、新罕布什尔州、芝加哥、爱荷华州的电话。

sentences.en: And I'm not talking about a call.
sentences.zh: 我指的不是一个电话。

sentences.en: I'm talking about many calls from these places.
sentences.zh: 我指的是来自这些地方的许多电话。

sentences.en: And women immediately started getting abortions.
sentences.zh: 女性们立刻开始做堕胎手术。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: We've had people who have come by bus.
sentences.zh: 我们有人坐长途汽车来。

sentences.en: Women started traveling to New York.
sentences.zh: 女性开始前往纽约。

sentences.en: By car and flying in so that we've been able to place those people also.
sentences.zh: 乘汽车和坐飞机来，所以我们也能够安顿那些人。

sentences.en: And women started organizing to make sure that women's experience would be a good experience and not a bad experience.
sentences.zh: 女性开始组织起来，确保女性的体验会是美好的体验而不是糟糕的体验。

sentences.en: And what did you think of that?
sentences.zh: 你对此有什么看法？

sentences.en: I was really excited that the law had changed and women would now be able to get abortions.
sentences.zh: 我真的很兴奋，法律已经改变了，女性现在能够做堕胎手术了。

sentences.en: That was very, very exciting.
sentences.zh: 那真是非常非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: I can't deny that I didn't have a little bit of disappointment that I would never be able to finish this litigation.
sentences.zh: 我不能否认，我有一点点失望，因为我再也无法完成这场诉讼了。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Because we knew we would have gone up to the Supreme Court and we could have been part of impacting the whole country and not just New York.
sentences.zh: 因为我们知道我们会一路打到最高法院，我们可以参与并影响整个国家，而不仅仅是纽约。

sentences.en: So, Nancy, it kind of sounds like you're saying doing it through the legislature was, in a way, more vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 所以，南希，听起来你是在说，通过立法机构来做，在某种程度上更加脆弱。

sentences.en: I mean, a kind of a weaker protection for abortion access than if it had gone through the courts, as you imagined.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，与你设想的通过法院途径相比，这对堕胎权的保护要薄弱一些。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为是这样的。

sentences.en: For one thing, if the composition of the legislature changes, they can change the law again.
sentences.zh: 一方面，如果立法机构的人员构成发生变化，他们可以再次修改法律。

sentences.en: If you can develop a constitutional basis, you hope that won't change.
sentences.zh: 如果你能建立一个宪法基础，你希望它不会改变。

sentences.en: The other thing is that it only applied to New York.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是它只适用于纽约。

sentences.en: That's exactly what I was going to say.
sentences.zh: 这正是我要说的。

sentences.en: That's the other thing.
sentences.zh: 还有另一件事。

sentences.en: It only applied to New York.
sentences.zh: 它只适用于纽约。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 我在“罗诉

sentences.en: My recollection is she told me about her client and that she was going to be going into court
sentences.zh: 我的记忆是，她跟我讲了她的客户，以及她即将出庭

sentences.en: and asked me if I would send her my papers that would outline the legal theories we were using.
sentences.zh: 并问我是否可以把概述我们当时所用法律理论的文件寄给她。

sentences.en: And what was different about her case compared to yours, Nancy?
sentences.zh: 南希，她的案子和你的有什么不同？

sentences.en: Well, hers was an individual pregnant woman
sentences.zh: 嗯，她的案子是一个怀孕的个人

sentences.en: Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the court.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官先生，法庭好。

sentences.en: who was looking to get an abortion and needed to go into court to obtain a temporary restraining order,
sentences.zh: 她寻求堕胎，需要出庭获得临时限制令，

sentences.en: which is not an easy thing to do, to block the law from being enforced against her.
sentences.zh: 要阻止法律针对她执行，这不是一件容易的事。

sentences.en: Jane Roe, the pregnant woman, had gone to several Dallas physicians seeking an abortion, but had been refused care because of the Texas law.
sentences.zh: 怀孕女性简·罗曾去找达拉斯的几位医师寻求堕胎，但由于德州法律而被拒绝提供医疗服务。

sentences.en: There were kernels of what we were arguing in New York, but it landed more on rights like privacy.
sentences.zh: 其中包含了我们在纽约争论的核心，但它更多地落脚于隐私等权利上。

sentences.en: This court said if the right of privacy is to mean anything, it is the right of the individual, whether married or single, to make determinations for themselves.
sentences.zh: 最高法院表示，如果隐私权有什么意义的话，那就是个人（无论是已婚还是未婚）为自己做决定的权利。

sentences.en: Privacy is a very passive right.
sentences.zh: 隐私是一个非常被动的权利。

sentences.en: You're just saying, you know, I need this realm around me that's private that the government can't get involved in.
sentences.zh: 你只是说，你知道的，我需要周围有这样一个私人领域，政府不能介入。

sentences.en: Liberty is saying, I have a life.
sentences.zh: 自由则是在说，我有一个人生。

sentences.en: I have to be able to live my life to the fulleSt.
sentences.zh: 我必须能够充分享受我的生活。

sentences.en: And unless you get off my body, I will not be able to live that active life.
sentences.zh: 除非你从我的身体上退开，否则我将无法过那种积极的生活。

sentences.en: It seems like Roe was based on an argument that's basically butt out.
sentences.zh: 看起来“罗诉韦德案”是基于一种基本上是“少管闲事”的论点。

sentences.en: This is my private space.
sentences.zh: 这是我的私人空间。

sentences.en: But your argument was deeper in a way, kind of based on, you know, this is a basic building block of being a free person.
sentences.zh: 但你的论点在某种程度上更深层，某种程度上基于，你知道的，这是一个自由人的基本组成部分。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.en: Sure.

sentences.zh: 在今天的一项里程碑式裁决中，最高法院将堕胎合法化了。

sentences.en: Nancy, can you tell me where you were when Roe was decided?
sentences.zh: 南希，你能告诉我宣判“罗诉韦德案”时你在哪里吗？

sentences.en: Thus, the anti-abortion laws of 46 states were rendered unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 因此，46个州的反对堕胎法被判定为违宪。

sentences.en: Unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 违宪。

sentences.en: Do you remember reading about it, how you felt?
sentences.zh: 你还记得阅读相关报道时的情景吗，你当时有什么感觉？

sentences.en: I was excited, relieved, and disappointed.
sentences.zh: 我很兴奋，感到释怀，同时也感到失望。

sentences.en: Okay, tell me about that.
sentences.zh: 好的，跟我说说那是怎么回事。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, I was excited that we now had a constitutional right to abortion.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我很高兴我们现在有了堕胎的宪法权利。

sentences.en: I was disappointed that we had to search for the right to liberty in it, that it wasn't front and center.
sentences.zh: 我感到失望的是，我们必须在其中搜寻自由权，它并不是核心和焦点。

sentences.en: And I also realized the way they did it was complicated and that that was going to present problems down the road.
sentences.zh: 我也意识到他们这样做很复杂，这将在未来带来问题。

sentences.en: I also knew, though, that there was a danger that it was going to be chipped away at it in different ways.
sentences.zh: 然而我也知道，存在着一种危险，即它会以各种方式被一点点剥夺。

sentences.en: And, of course, that's exactly what happened.
sentences.zh: 当然，这正是发生的事情。

sentences.en: Was it a nagging thought for you, Nancy, that, you know, your argument might have been the better argument?
sentences.zh: 南希，你是否一直有一个挥之不去的想法，就是说，你的论点可能才是更好的论点？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Other people have suggested it.
sentences.zh: 其他人也这么提过。

sentences.en: In terms of where we are today,
sentences.zh: 就我们今天的处境而言，

sentences.en: I will be honest, I don't think it would have made one whit of difference because the people who have struck down the right to abortion would have just said,
sentences.zh: 老实说，我认为这不会产生哪怕一点点影响，因为那些推翻堕胎权的人会说，

sentences.en: well, women didn't have a right to equal protection when the Constitution was founded.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当宪法创立时，女性并没有平等保护的权利。

sentences.en: I guess, Nancy, you know, you're saying that the other side now would say that women just don't have rights in the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 我想，南希，你知道的，你是在说另一方现在会认为女性在宪法中根本没有权利。

sentences.en: That's a very radical argument, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常激进的论点，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it feels like it would have been harder to argue against your argument that they had, right, you know, that this was their liberty that was being taken away from them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，感觉要反驳你的论点会更难，你知道的，即这是她们被剥夺的自由。

sentences.en: In that sense, yeah, but because none of this came up in the Constitution,
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，是的，但因为这些在宪法中都没有提及，

sentences.en: none of it's legitimate from the perspective of the people who just took away our rights.
sentences.zh: 从那些刚刚剥夺了我们权利的人的角度来看，这一切都是不合法的。

sentences.en: the society has changed in so many ways that you can't count them.
sentences.zh: 社会已经发生了无数次变化。

sentences.en: So to say there was no right to abortion in the Constitution then, and therefore there is none now, it's just bogus, frankly.
sentences.zh: 因此，说当时宪法中没有堕胎权，所以现在也没有，坦率地说，这完全是胡扯。

sentences.en: I don't know how to treat it with any, even intellectual, dignity.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该如何以任何哪怕是理智的尊严来对待它。

sentences.en: I mean, beyond whether your argument was legally more solid, do you think a Supreme Court ruling based on women's equality would have been any less divisive than Roe has been?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，撇开你的论点在法律上是否更坚实不谈，你认为基于女性平等的最高法院裁决会比“罗诉韦德案”带来的分裂更少吗？

sentences.en: I mean, would that have been a less controversial, less divisive argument?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那会是一个争议更少、分裂更小的论点吗？

sentences.en: No, people don't want to deal with the fact that what was divisive about Roe v.
sentences.zh: 不，人们不想正视这样一个事实：关于“罗诉韦德案”引发分裂的原因，并非在于它的裁决方式。

sentences.en: Wade was not the way in which it was decided.
sentences.zh: 问题在于堕胎本身。

sentences.en: It's abortion.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个非常分裂的社会，但实际上这种分裂是宗教分裂。

sentences.en: We have a society that is very divided, but really the division is a religious division.
sentences.zh: 最激烈的人并不是因为女性在社会中的地位而如此激烈。

sentences.en: The people who are most vehement are not that vehement because of women's place in society.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以如此激烈，是因为他们真诚地、坚信不移地认为——而且我认为他们应该永远这样认为，因为这是他们的信仰——胎儿从受孕的那一刻起就是一个人，

sentences.en: They are that vehement because they truly, firmly believe, and I think they should believe it forever because it's their belief that a fetus is a human being
sentences.zh: 我们不能终结胎儿的生命，而它伤害女性这一事实是无关紧要的。

sentences.en: for the moment of conception, that we cannot terminate fetal life, and that the fact that it harms women is irrelevant.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种深厚根植的宗教信仰，我尊重他们的宗教信仰。

sentences.en: But it is a deeply held religious belief, and I respect their religious belief.
sentences.zh: 我不同意，但我尊重它。

sentences.en: I don't agree with it, but I respect it.
sentences.zh: 我不接受的是，他们的宗教信仰应该能够控制女性的生活。

sentences.en: What I do not accept is that their religious belief should be able to control what happens to women's lives.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: That's the problem.
